name: Rutz
review: Berlin's sole three-star flagship delivers Marco Müller's "Inspiration" tasting menu—a 12- to 13-course journey shaped by hyper-regional Brandenburg suppliers, wild-foraged herbs, and effortless precision. Standouts like Oldenburg Wagyu with beef garum and North Sea squid with red cabbage pair with an acclaimed wine cellar in an unexpectedly relaxed, warm setting.

name: CODA
review: Behind an unassuming Neukölln facade, René Frank redefines fine dining by applying patisserie techniques across a 13- to 15-course tasting menu—completely free of refined sugar. Every savoury-adjacent and dessert course arrives with a bespoke drink pairing in a dimly lit, laid-back dining room with open-kitchen counter seats.

name: FACIL
review: An airy fifth-floor rooftop oasis inside The Mandala Hotel, framed by wraparound glass, bamboo plants, and a serene courtyard terrace. Michael Kempf and Joachim Gerner craft five- to eight-course menus uniting classic French technique with Mediterranean and Asian accents, backed by a masterful sommelier team.

name: Horváth
review: Set along Kreuzberg's leafy Landwehrkanal with historic wood panelling, a Jim Avignon mural, and a glass-fronted kitchen. Sebastian Frank places regional vegetables at the heart of his Austrian-rooted avant-garde cooking—celebrating craft over luxury clichés in dishes like "celery ripe & young" alongside Eastern European and Austrian wines.

name: Tim Raue
review: Berlin-born Tim Raue's sleek Kreuzberg flagship pairs unmistakable Berlin boldness with intense Asian-inspired aromatics—balancing heat, sweetness, and acidity without dairy, white sugar, or heavy starches. Iconic plates like Wasabi Langoustine and Duck "Marie-Anne" headline the "Kolibri x Berlin", "Koi", and vegan tasting menus.

name: Bandol sur mer
review: Housed in a tiny, dimly lit former kebab shop on bustling Torstraße, Bandol sur mer pairs vintage East Berlin shabby-chic charm with fiercely inventive cooking. Andreas Saul's seven-course regional omnivore and vegetarian menus showcase house fermentations, smoking, carrot charcuterie, and subtle Far Eastern notes.

name: Bonvivant
review: Berlin's first purely vegan Michelin-starred cocktail bistro proves plant-based haute cuisine lacks nothing. Driven by Brandenburg produce cooked "from leaf to root" and fermented in-house, Nikodemus Berger serves six- and seven-course seasonal menus alongside inventive cocktail pairings in a warm Schöneberg setting.

name: Bricole
review: An intimate, neighbourly eight-table bistro in Prenzlauer Berg where proprietor-sommelier Fabian Fischer champions over 300 German, Austrian, and French wines. Chef Steven Zeidler elevates classic French technique with nuanced Asian accents—such as Nordic halibut with shiso and dashi, or guinea fowl with kombu and sour cherries.

name: Cookies Cream
review: Quintessential Berlin hidden fine dining: ring the bell behind an unmarked courtyard door and climb into a former nightclub turned industrial-chic loft. Five- to seven-course strictly vegetarian menus (with vegan options and iconic Parmesan dumplings) shine alongside vibrant wine and non-alcoholic pairings.

name: GOLVET
review: Perched on the eighth floor of the Loeser & Wolff building with sweeping views over Potsdamer Platz and an open-kitchen counter. Chef Nicholas Hahn gives vegetables, fish, and meat a bold, creative twist—such as pointed cabbage with smoked eel and Koshihikari, or John Dory with horseradish and kohlrabi.

name: hallmann & klee
review: Overlooking Neukölln's village-like Böhmischer Platz with a lively summer terrace and warm, understated interior. Chef-patron Sarah Hallmann delivers streamlined, punchy modern dishes crafted from superb ingredients—highlights include the signature "potato, lovage, whey" and halibut with champagne and Périgord truffle.

name: Hugos
review: Crowning the 14th floor of InterContinental Berlin with panoramic views over Tiergarten and the city skyline, Hugos has held a Michelin star continuously since 1999. Chef Johannes Gehrich crafts refined six- and eight-course menus—like snow crab with imperial caviar and Dover sole with vin jaune and morels—paired with polished service.

name: Irma la Douce
review: Bathed in warm golden light with old-world elegance and laid-back charm, Irma la Douce brings undogmatic French savoir-vivre to Potsdamer Straße. Expect melt-in-the-mouth bœuf bourguignon, signature Carbonara nodding to the chef's roots, classic crème brûlée, and a standout French-focused wine list, plus weekday lunch.

name: Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer
review: Inside the grand Hotel Adlon Kempinski—with coveted tables overlooking the Brandenburg Gate—Jonas Zörner contrasts opulent historic heritage with modern, creative cooking rooted in a classic French foundation. Offered as five- or six-course menus or à la carte Signatures, accompanied by over 1,600 wine labels.

name: Loumi
review: Self-taught chef Karl-Louis Kömmler leads a young team in a minimalist, counter-focused Kreuzberg corner space. Breaking culinary conventions with strong Japanese influences across an eight-course menu, Loumi's signature crispy veal sweetbread with Kaluga caviar and habanero sauce delivers bold, pared-down harmony.

name: Matthias
review: Occupying a stylish Kollwitzkiez corner building with earthy woods and a signature terracotta counter, Silvio Pfeufer, Janine Woltaire, and sommelier Michael Stiel present a modern, ingredient-led take on French cuisine. Choose five- or six-course omnivore or vegetarian menus—or dine à la carte.

name: Nobelhart & Schmutzig
review: Billy Wagner and Micha Schäfer's "brutally local" manifesto celebrates exclusively Berlin and Brandenburg ingredients—no pepper, lemons, or imported olive oil, only extraordinary seasonal produce and house-churned butter. Seated around the open kitchen counter, guests enjoy six- or eight-course menus with natural wines and beers.

name: pars Restaurant
review: An intimate, art-filled Charlottenburg dining room founded by sculptor and master confectioner Kristiane Kegelmann. From the communal table overlooking the open kitchen, savour Florian Sperlhofer's finely balanced seasonal dishes—like smoked local eel with beetroot or pike-perch with fermented cabbage—finished with house-crafted pralines.

name: tulus lotrek
review: Inside a high-stuccoed Graefekiez apartment adorned with bold art and quirky wallpaper, Ilona Scholl leads warm, exuberant hospitality while Maximilian Strohe builds deeply flavoursome eight-course omnivore and vegetarian menus—from Arctic char with veal tongue to carabinero prawn with gochujang and candied ginger.

name: Barra
review: A buzzy, pared-back Neukölln neighborhood favorite where seasonal European sharing plates shine with bold, focused flavors. Menus change constantly around top-notch produce, natural wines, and effortless hospitality—book well ahead for a seat at the lively bar or timber tables.

name: CHEZ NASSIB
review: Newly awarded a 2026 Bib Gourmand (formerly Byblos), this warm, stylish Wilmersdorf dining room brings vibrant Lebanese and Mediterranean cooking to the table. Expect silky mezze, aromatic charcoal-grilled dishes, and generous, authentic hospitality at outstanding value.

name: Lucky Leek
review: One of Berlin's pioneering purely plant-based fine-casual addresses, earning a long-standing Bib Gourmand for creative, beautifully plated three- or five-course vegan menus. Colorful seasonal compositions and warm Prenzlauer Berg charm make it a delight for vegans and omnivores alike.

name: MaMi's
review: A charming, bustling food-and-wine spot on Oderberger Straße run with genuine warmth by Marcel and Miriam Hertrampf. Modern, internationally inspired sharing plates are crafted with sharp technique and paired with an expressive, thoughtfully curated wine list.

name: MASTAN
review: An intimate, atmospheric Kreuzberg bistro where chef Yann Mastantuono celebrates soulful French gastronomy with top-notch produce and rich, deeply crafted sauces. Classic dishes and an exceptional French wine selection deliver authentic Parisian bistro spirit at Bib Gourmand value.

name: November Brasserie
review: A chic, wood-lined contemporary Japanese brasserie off Kollwitzplatz blending minimalist aesthetics with lively evening energy. Expect refined izakaya-inspired plates, delicate sashimi, grilled specialties, and thoughtfully matched sake and cocktails.

name: Nußbaumerin
review: A beloved Charlottenburg gem run by Johanna Nußbaumer since 2008, offering cozy, unpretentious Alpine hospitality and immaculate Austrian classics. From crisp Wiener Schnitzel and hearty soups to homemade desserts and fine Austrian wines, every plate radiates care.

name: Remi
review: Housed inside the sleek Suhrkamp publishing building with floor-to-ceiling windows and a central open kitchen, Remi serves pleasingly clear, seasonal feel-good plates without unnecessary flourishes—from fennel risotto with radicchio to mackerel with corn and tomatillo, plus a sought-after summer terrace.

name: Salhino
review: A new 2026 Bib Gourmand winner celebrating family-run West Georgian and Megrelian cooking in Charlottenburg. Handmade khinkali dumplings, bubbling khachapuri, walnut-spiced vegetable dishes, and rare Georgian amber wines make for a soulful feast.

Drawing on his Peruvian heritage and life in Italy, chef Matias Diaz weaves produce from both countries into the '136 Experience Menü', a creative set menu changing every two months (with a vegetarian option) inside a charming vintage-styled Mitte dining room with summer pavement tables.

name: 893 Ryotei
review: Behind a mirrored, graffiti-tagged Kantstraße facade awaits a sleek, moody black interior pulsing around an open kitchen. The Duc Ngo fuses Japanese craft with Asian, South American, and European accents—from impeccable sashimi and tempura to signature sashimi taquitos and unagi royal.

name: aerde
review: Set inside the striking Robertneun-designed building at Lokdepot, this minimalist, design-forward restaurant champions nature-rooted seasonal cooking. Produce from Brandenburg farms and thoughtful fermentations shape deeply aromatic, unhurried modern menus.

name: Bardele
review: An effortlessly cool Mitte ristorante and bar reinterpreting classic cucina povera and regional Italian traditions with modern Berlin polish. Handmade pastas, crisp seasonal plates, and a sharp wine and aperitivo program keep Auguststraße humming.

name: Berta
review: Acclaimed chef Assaf Granit brings the vibrant flavors of Jerusalem to Kreuzberg in a high-energy, warmly lit room. Generous sharing plates reinterpret family recipes with bold spices, wood-fired aromas, and inventive cocktails.

name: Bieberbau Berlin
review: Set in a heritage-listed 1894 dining room adorned with extraordinary stucco work by Richard Bieber, chef Stephan Garkisch and hostess-sommelier Anne Garkisch deliver modern set menus where garden-grown herbs and spices take center stage.

name: Bob & Thoms
review: An unaffected two-man gem on a quiet street near Viktoria-Luise-Platz: host Oliver Körber brings genuine Berlin warmth while chef Ruben Pahl crafts classically grounded five-course menus—from velvety lobster soup to rosy saddle of venison—in an intimate room with a lovely summer terrace.

name: Bocca di Bacco
review: A long-standing Mitte institution blending late-19th-century grandeur with polished Italian hospitality on Friedrichstraße. Classic regional pastas, pristine seafood, and an encyclopedic Italian cellar make it a perennial favorite for business lunches and lively dinners.

name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
review: Steps from KaDeWe, Tim Raue's chic French brasserie channels Parisian elegance with vibrant, contemporary seasoning. Classic dishes like steak tartare, bouillabaisse, and Königsberger-style twists arrive in a gleaming, bustling dining room.

name: Brasserie Lamazère
review: Authentic French brasserie flair in the heart of Charlottenburg, complete with a charming wine terrace and warm, convivial service. Market-fresh French classics and a well-chosen Gallic cellar deliver timeless neighborhood appeal.

name: BRIKZ
review: In a sleek, wood-and-brick Charlottenburg space near Savignyplatz, Arne Anker crafts seasonal casual-fine-dining tasting menus rooted in farm-to-table produce. Expect sharp, playful flavor pairings, precise sauces, and an inviting open-kitchen energy.

name: CARTE BLANCHE
review: Tucked inside the elegant SO/ Berlin Das Stue hotel on the leafy edge of Tiergarten, CARTE BLANCHE pairs plush, design-led surroundings with refined French brasserie classics and international touches, plus a serene garden terrace overlooking the zoo.

name: Château Royal
review: Inside Mitte's art-filled boutique hotel of the same name, chef Philipp Walther serves sun-drenched, produce-driven Mediterranean cooking with crisp modern restraint, backed by a sharp wine list and cosmopolitan salon atmosphere.

name: Crackers
review: Located one floor below Cookies Cream in a former theatre hall off Friedrichstraße: ring the bell and walk past the bustling kitchen into a dimly lit, high-ceilinged dining room serving ambitious meat, fish, and vegetable plates alongside stellar cocktails.

name: Dae Mon
review: A chic, stylish Mitte address on Monbijouplatz spotlighting open-minded Asian-European fusion. Delicate Korean and Japanese techniques meet seasonal European ingredients across finely balanced tasting menus and creative sake and wine pairings.

name: Diekmann
review: A West Berlin classic since 1982 in a wood-paneled historic space just off Kurfürstendamm. Celebrated for its oyster bar, refined French-German staples, and timeless white-tablecloth hospitality.

name: eins44
review: Tucked into the third courtyard of the Otto-Reichel-Höfe inside a converted distillery, eins44 pairs industrial urban-loft charm and solid beechwood tables with ingredient-led five- or seven-course seasonal menus—both omnivore and vegetarian—at remarkable value.

name: Fa:me
review: An intimate Neukölln gastrobar blending contemporary fine-dining craft with relaxed neighborhood spirit. Mediterranean-inflected modern plates—offered à la carte or as a convivial sharing menu—are matched with expressive wines.

name: FUKAGAWA - Fine Dining
review: In a serene Kreuzberg dining room, chefs Felix Thoms and Leonardo Tsubasa Donati bridge Japanese precision with European seasonal produce. Elegant tasting menus and refined à la carte plates showcase delicate dashi, pristine fish, and sake pairings.

name: Fukagawa Ramen XBerg
review: A minimalist, bustling Kreuzberg ramen bar where booking ahead pays off at both lunch and dinner. Deeply layered broths like matured soy-sauce shoyu ramen with handmade noodles, crisp gyoza starters, and a notable sake and cocktail list shine.

name: Funky Fisch
review: The Duc Ngo's lively Kantstraße seafood hub spotlights pristine fish and shellfish displayed right at the center of the stylish room. Dishes span crisp Asian-accented crudo, lobster rolls, and classic European seafood favorites.

name: GRACE
review: Glamorous, cosmopolitan dining inside Hotel Zoo Berlin on Kurfürstendamm. Beneath dramatic brickwork and velvet accents, the kitchen turns out modern European dishes infused with bold Asian spices, complemented by one of City West's sleekest cocktail bars.

name: INDIA CLUB
review: Germany's first Indian restaurant recognized by the Michelin Guide, nestled inside the Adlon Palais steps from the Brandenburg Gate. Chef Manish Bahukhandi showcases refined North Indian cooking—aromatic curries, tandoor specialties, and warm, plush elegance.

name: Jäger & Lustig
review: A characterful Friedrichshain tavern, beer parlor, and leafy beer garden elevating traditional German and Brandenburg Heimatküche. Expect carefully sourced game, seasonal comfort classics, and welcoming old-school hospitality.

name: JAJA
review: One of Neukölln's trailblazing natural-wine bistros, pairing a deep, adventurous cellar with vibrant, locally sourced organic small plates. The laid-back, convivial atmosphere and crisp, inventive flavors make it a magnet for Berlin wine lovers.

name: Julius Ernst
review: The sleek, minimalist Wedding sibling to ernst blends youthful, laid-back energy with razor-sharp French-Japanese craft. Watch the open counter turn out intensely flavorful omakase and à la carte dishes—from rose shrimp with nori and yuzu to grilled scallop with squash—plus weekend breakfast and pastries.

name: Kitchen Library
review: A warm, personal Charlottenburg casual-fine-dining address where Udo and Daniela Knörlein pair uncompromising ingredient quality with expressive modern French craftsmanship and thoughtful wine recommendations.

name: Kitten Deli
review: Bringing Tel Aviv energy to Neukölln's Friedelstraße, this lively corner deli serves silky hummus bowls, roasted vegetables, warm house-baked challah, and bright North African and Levantine small plates.

name: Kurpfalz Weinstuben
review: A treasured Charlottenburg wine tavern steeped in Palatinate tradition since 1934. Wood-paneled parlors, generous regional German cooking, and an enviable cellar of German Rieslings and Pinots create enduring charm.

name: Li.Ke Thai Vegan
review: A vibrant, colorful Friedrichshain favorite showcasing 100% vegan Thai cooking inspired by street-food classics. Fragrant yellow lemongrass curries, pad thai, and balanced sweet-spicy aromas shine in a cheerful, relaxed room.

name: Long March Canteen
review: A cool, dimly lit Kreuzberg hot spot with an open kitchen turning out handmade Cantonese dim sum, dumplings, and genuinely spicy sharing dishes—available à la carte or as convivial group menus alongside craft cocktails and wines.

name: Lovis
review: Set inside the dramatically restored courtyards of the historic Wilmina former women's prison, chef Sophia Rudolph crafts vibrant contemporary German cuisine with bold vegetable-forward elegance, served in a luminous architectural oasis.

name: Macionga
review: A stylish neighborhood restaurant and wine bar near Olivaer Platz from sommelier André Macionga and chef Christopher Wecker. Clear, seasonal European plates pair seamlessly with an outstanding, wide-ranging cellar.

name: Madame Ngo - Une Brasserie Hanoi
review: Blending Hanoi street-food heritage with French brasserie polish on Kantstraße, The Duc Ngo's lively dining room is famed for its aromatic pho broths, crisp banh mi, delicate spring rolls, and convivial all-day buzz.

name: merold
review: Recognized with a Michelin Green Star for its Bioland-certified, 90% organic sourcing, Jonas Merold's intimate Neukölln restaurant pairs global culinary craftsmanship with deeply flavorful Berlin-Brandenburg seasonal produce.

name: MINE
review: Steps from Kurfürstendamm, MINE delivers self-styled 'fun fine dining' with contemporary Italian flair. House-made pastas, refined meat and seafood plates, and a buzzing cocktail bar create a vibrant evening hotspot.

name: NaNum
review: Part ceramic gallery, part intimate Korean dining room: singer and ceramicist Jinok Kim serves multi-course contemporary Korean menus rich in house-made ferments on her own handmade stoneware.

name: Norms
review: Right next to Volkspark am Weinbergsweg, Björn Swanson, Norman Faust, and Sabine Panzer-Faust elevate German comfort cooking 'like grandma used to make'—lighter and more refined, from smoked pork croquettes and Kiel sprats to Königsberger Klopse, paired with expert wine advice.

name: Orania.Berlin
review: Centered around a glowing open show-kitchen and Steinway grand piano at Oranienplatz, chef Philipp Vogel blends cosmopolitan Asian-European finesse with Kreuzberg soul—famed especially for his multi-course Peking-style X-Berg Duck.

name: OTSUKA
review: Hidden inside a Nordbahnhof building that also houses an organic supermarket, perhaps Berlin's smallest restaurant seats just a handful of guests at a minimalist ash-wood counter for an authentic, affordably priced nigiri omakase crafted piece by piece before your eyes.

name: Otto
review: A tiny, lively Prenzlauer Berg neighborhood favorite where chef Vadim Otto Ursus celebrates hyper-seasonal Brandenburg produce, house preserves, and wild herbs in concise, deeply expressive plates paired with natural wines.

name: Oukan
review: Hidden behind a red door in a quiet Mitte courtyard, Oukan fuses Buddhist Shojin Ryori temple philosophy with contemporary plant-based fine dining—delicate umami-rich vegan courses paired with rare teas, sake, and low-intervention wines.

images.caption: Vegan Japanese Fine Dining · Michelin Guide

name: POTS
review: Relaxed, chic, and stylish inside The Ritz-Carlton, featuring striking copper-accented decor and a large open kitchen. Chefs put a modern spin on traditional German cuisine—like Königsberger Klopse with yellow beetroot—alongside sharing plates and a surprise menu.

name: Rutz - Zollhaus
review: Set in an idyllic historic brick customs house along the leafy Landwehr Canal, the casual sister to three-star Rutz serves deeply flavorful modern German cooking and classic comfort dishes backed by an extraordinary German wine cellar.

name: SKYKITCHEN
review: Perched on the 12th floor of Vienna House Andel's with sweeping Berlin skyline views and vintage-meets-urban decor, SKYKITCHEN serves five-course 'Voyage Culinaire' and vegetarian tasting menus paired with an Eastern European-focused wine list.

name: Stoke
review: Chef Jeff Claudio's acclaimed Japanese-inspired charcoal-and-woodfire restaurant in Kreuzberg elevates yakitori skewers and open-fire seasonal plates with crisp technique, binchotan smoke, and a lively counter atmosphere.

name: VOX Restaurant
review: Inside the Grand Hyatt at Potsdamer Platz, this sleek, spacious dining room unites an acclaimed authentic sushi counter with contemporary seasonal cooking—available à la carte or as a five-course menu—plus an iconic whisky and cocktail bar.

images.caption: Open Kitchen & Sushi Bar · Grand Hyatt
